rubric.contrast: Legend text is black on white at about 21:1, far above 4.5:1. The blue data stroke measures 5.37:1 and the grey dashed stroke better than 3:1 against white at the delivered 1399x720 size, so neither series is lost to low contrast.
rubric.data_ink: Only data ink is present: eight contour levels drawn twice from one shared array, one black vessel outline, one marker pair per series in two sets, and two legend swatches. A colour census of the PNG gives 15,566 pixels of the exact stroke colour #3366cc against 1,208 black and about 1,947 grey pixels including the dashed stroke and its antialiasing, so the drawn data are the weight on the page.
rubric.decoration: No stylisation on the canvas. Axes are off, so there are no spines, ticks, tick labels or gridlines; the background is plain white, the legend is frameless and unboxed, and there is no title, gradient or shaded band.
rubric.label_collision: The whole legend occupies x 465-930 on the 1399 px width and y 24-43 on the 720 px height, with a clear 41 px gap between the two entries, and the topmost data ink begins at y 90, so no label is clipped and no label overlaps another label or a contour. No ink touches a canvas edge. The only overlaps on the canvas are between the two null-marker sets themselves, recorded as finding 2; the legend-specific decode problem is finding 1.
rubric.legibility: A single diverted poloidal cross-section is centred in the middle third of the canvas, drawn as nested closed contours in solid blue (#3366cc) over an almost coincident set of dashed grey (#555555) contours, enclosed by a thin black vessel outline and marked with a triangle at the magnetic axis and a cross at the lower X-point. A two-entry frameless legend sits above the panel: a blue line with a triangle marker labelled 'stalled bank state' and a grey dashed line with a triangle marker labelled 'analytic oracle'. Where the two fields differ, most plainly along the top-right and upper-left of the outer contours, the core reads apart; in the core they coincide and the blue covers the grey, which is the agreement the caption claims rather than a hidden difference. What does not read at a glance: the marker vocabulary (triangle means axis, cross means saddle) is neither on the canvas nor in the caption, both legend handles carry a triangle although the contours carry no markers, the two marker sets at each null collapse into one composite mark, and the solid blue contour is broken into isolated short strokes along the top of the outer level and at the lower right, where it reads as a dashed line and can pass for the oracle encoding.
rubric.table_form: The figure shows flux contours in poloidal cross-section, the vessel boundary and the positions of stationary points. That is a spatial relationship; nothing in the image is a picture of tabular information, and the page carries the residual and factor results as tables beside it.

findings.summary: The legend keys the strokes but not the marks, and it keys the marks wrongly. Both handles are built with marker='^' (line 120 and line 129), so the 'stalled bank state' entry shows a blue line carrying a triangle although the plotted contours carry no markers at all, and both entries show the same triangle while the plotted null vocabulary uses a triangle for the magnetic axis and a cross for the admitted saddle. A reader can tell which colour belongs to which state but cannot learn from the figure that the triangle marks the axis and the cross the saddle, and may read the legend triangles as markers on the contour lines. Non-blocking: the contours and marker colours remain identifiable and the caption carries the residual.

The two null-marker sets collapse into one composite mark each, so the agreement between the solved and analytic null positions cannot be read from the figure. At the axis the smaller blue triangle is drawn over the larger grey oracle triangle, leaving grey visible only as a thin rim; at the lower X-point the grey oracle cross and the blue solved cross overlap into one dark blocky mark. The caption's 'larger grey oracle markers behind them' describes the drawing scheme accurately, but the render does not let a reader resolve two markers or measure the offset between them. Non-blocking: both null sets are present and their colours distinguish them, and the page does not claim a numeric null agreement.

The contour levels are never stated to the reader. Eight levels are computed from a shared array and drawn twice, but their values are emitted only on the renderer's stdout; neither the legend, the axis (switched off) nor the caption gives a flux value for any line, and the caption says only that eight physical levels are shared. A reader of the evidence page sees a shape comparison but cannot say what flux a contour represents or relate the panel to the residual and factor tables beside it. Non-blocking: the figure's stated purpose is the comparison between the two states, which survives without level values.

The cross-section is drawn small on a wide canvas. The plotted data occupy x 512-892 of the 1399 px width, about 27 percent, with the outer thirds of the figure empty on both sides; the cause is an equal-aspect poloidal panel on the mandated 14x7.2 inch slide canvas, not a choice about the data. At the delivered size the contour spacing is drawn at roughly a quarter of the width the figure actually has, which is why the near-coincident blue and grey lines need looking at rather than reading at a glance. Non-blocking: every contour is still resolvable.

The solid solved contour is not continuous, and in places it reads as the dashed oracle encoding. Along the top of the outer level the blue stroke appears as several isolated short segments with white gaps, and at the lower right a contour ends in a flat butt end at about (697, 652) while an inboard segment begins abruptly at about (522, 204), both well inside the black vessel line and clear of any marker; the cause is a scattered-node contour whose support ends and fragments before the vessel. A reader can mistake a broken solid stroke for the dashed analytic series and so misread agreement or disagreement exactly where the two fields differ. Non-blocking: no plotted value is withheld and the truncation is confined to the outer levels.

item_verdicts.byte_identity: The figure blob b856e66e8149 and the renderer blob 63a7c03c26e8 are identical at heads 425d44581fee, f210e2c81344 and 703cfaab5a8c, and the caption at fragment line 38 is unchanged between the last two, so a reader can compare this verdict with the earlier figure reviews on the same artwork.
item_verdicts.caption_independence: The caption is not a restatement of a title; the figure carries no title. It states the encoding (solid blue solved, dashed grey oracle, black vessel), the shared eight-level comparison, the marker colours, the plotting state's solved-equation residual 1.0349e-2 with converged=false, and the caveat that close contour overlap does not imply convergence. Its marker sentence explains colour but not shape, and it does not warn that the solid stroke is broken in places, which are findings 1 and 5.
item_verdicts.finding_materiality: Five non-blocking findings and no blocking finding. Nothing is clipped, no text is unreadable, and no plotted value is withheld: both contour series and both null-marker colours appear on the canvas, and the caption carries the residual numerically. Each finding is a readability or decoding cost that does not stop a reader reading the figure.
item_verdicts.rendered_artifact: The single attached figure was opened and inspected as an image at native 1399x720, plus magnified crops of that same PNG; no SVG and no other image was read.
item_verdicts.scope: Read-only. No file was edited, created, moved, deleted, redrawn, relabelled or reformatted; the only writes are this record at its two declared paths and the run manifest.
